title: Waiting for a turn inside a peer game is listed at age 5
summary: CDC says most children follow rules or wait their turn when they play games with other children, by about age 5.
body: Social milestones at 5 years include following rules or taking turns when playing games with other children. The partner is a peer, and the structure is a game with a rule, not a baby sound-swap. CDC's most is 75 percent or more. A teaching table that prints taking turns beside the year 3 comes from another book and another cutoff. These US sheets are not a diagnosis.
